content.text:
**Finding: compliant (no redline).**

§ 22 satisfies the AUDIT rule at the **preferred** level on every element:

| Preferred element | Where met |
|---|---|
| Once per 12 months | 22.1 — "no more than once in any twelve-month period" |
| 30 days' written notice | 22.1 — "at least thirty days' prior written notice" |
| Business hours | 22.1 — "during normal business hours" |
| Independent auditor | 22.1 — "by an independent auditor" |
| Auditor confidentiality-bound | 22.1 — "bound by confidentiality" |
| Off-site where possible | 22.1 — "off-site where practicable" |
| Vendor cost unless >5% underpayment | 22.2 — cost shifts only on "underpayment exceeding five percent" |
| No direct system access | 22.2 — "may not access Customer systems directly" |

§ 22.3 adds further Customer-favourable protection (findings are Customer Confidential Information, use limited to enforcement, shortfall payment resolves the issue). I also checked the only other records-style heading, § 23 (Records and Customer Assurance), and the broader document for inspection/verification/remote-access rights binding us — there is no additional or competing Vendor audit route. Nothing to redline.
